name: Irene Baines
life: “I still remember holding a helm after another person's bad news.” On Sunday, near the bank steps, Irene takes a few minutes to read the public notices, especially the ones written in a hurry.
voice: I served under the skipper. She kept steering with a broken heart after her wife's death, so stopping now is hers to choose.
appearance: Back on the street, look for a gray fisher's sweater and one cuff folded back twice. Irene has a scattering of freckles across the bridge of the nose, with a center part and straight chestnut hair. Irene touches a knuckle to the chin when searching for a word during a conversation.
personality: Irene finds it easier to own up to a mistake than to accept praise. The worse the mistake, the more precise the account of exactly when it happened.
agenda: To give the former skipper room to choose.
family: Frankie Reyes is Irene’s cousin. Irene chooses the music. Frankie puts the kettle on. The cups come out before either brings up the reason for the visit. They trust a difficult conversation more if it has had an ordinary beginning. Asked about *One clean day*, Frankie says, “I took a call during the photograph. My friends left a space and took another after I came back.”
connections: Mika Lam. The outgoing skipper's deckhand and the successor compare how to honor the old routine.

reactions.situation: The new skipper changes the departure routine
reactions.response: Irene gives the new skipper space to explain the change before measuring it against the former routine.

reactions.situation: A family supper turns into an argument about old debt
reactions.response: Irene clears the dishes, lets the angriest speaker cool off, and resumes the conversation with a smaller audience.
